chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abdullah ibn Usman, that he saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
He trimmed his moustache until he pressed it against the palate.

key_terms.بِالْعَسِيبِ: Against the palate (roof of the mouth)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on trimming the moustache based on the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the physical precision of Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) grooming, where the moustache was trimmed so closely it adhered to the palate, distinguishing it from the beard. In Shia fiqh, this serves as the definitive evidence for the recommendation (mustahabb) of shortening the moustache while keeping the beard, reflecting the Prophet’s tradition of fitting natural beauty with modesty. The chain of transmission through Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah underscores the reliability of this practice within the early scholarly circles of Kufa.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abdullah Bin Usman that he saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
press his<sup>asws</sup> moustache until it was pasted like a palm branch’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain persons of his people from Ali ibn Asbat from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Uthman who had seen abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam,
trim his mustache up to the root of the hairs.”’
